Commentary.Commentary: Pakistan are firmly in the driver's seat as things stand. Still a lot of time left in this game, as we're only halfway through the second day. Pretty sure they would like to extend their lead to 400-450 at the very least. Might be difficult, as the track is turning. Will be interesting to see how the Australian bowlers go about their business. And will the Pakistan batsmen stand firm this time out? We'll find out soon when the third innings begins.

There were only two instances when Australia looked comfortable. One when Aaron Finch was in the middle and the other when Mitchell Starc provided a flurry of runs with Marnus Labuschagne towards the end. Other than that, no other batsman looked like they had the stomach to put up a fight. Before the end of Day 1, they lost last match's hero Usman Khawaja and nightwatchman Peter Siddle, and today followed more of the same. Not a pretty sight for any Aussie fan as they had to witness another collapse.

A wonderful bowling performance from the hosts as they have run right through the Australian batting line-up. Mohammad Abbas leading the charge against the Kangaroos once again, picked up a 5-fer and got things going as he demolished the top order. Shah and Asif joined in sharing 4 wickets between them and wrapped things up.

OUT! He's gone and that spells the end of the visitors' innings. A 5-wicket haul for Mohammad Abbas, well-deserved. He comes from around the wicket and fires in a yorker on middle and leg, angling in. Starc can't dig it out and it goes behind past the leg stump. Pakistan appeal, because they think it's caught Starc's boot on the way back and take the DRS. It's taken upstairs and replays show that it indeed did and the left-hander is gone. AUSTRALIA ARE BOWLED OUT FOR 145 AND CONCEDE A LEAD OF 137 RUNS!
Review taken for an lbw decision against Mitchell Starc. Is he gone?
Short and banged in quite close to off, Starc arches back a bit and places it to backward point.
The southpaw does well to leave that bouncer.
Lovely drive on the up through cover by Starc. He gets nicely on top of the bounce and caresses this drive beautifully for a brace.
The right-hander has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Slower one but still a bit too short, Jon keeps it out.
He waits inside his crease this time to defend this flatter one off the back foot.
A bit too full and Jon easily blocks it out.
Slower and a bit shorter, Starc goes back and pushes this towards mid on to get off strike.
Very full ball on off, blocked out off the front foot into covers.
Shorter and wider of off, allows Starc to tap it into the vacant point region and retain strike for the next over.
Comes around the wicket to the southpaw and fires in a length ball around off, angling in to Starc. Mitchell does well in defending it from his crease.

Marginally shorter of a good length around off. The ball hits the deck and nips back in slight, thereby taking the inside edge of Jon's bat. The ball rolls down towards square leg and the pair has taken a single.
Varies his length and bangs it in short. Holland sways back and lets it go through.
Similar ball and kept out safely by the no. 11 batsman off the back foot.
Starts a new spell with a good length ball around off. Jon does well to block it out.
Mohammad Abbas back on.
Driven through mid on for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Safe! It is indeed way down leg. Spinning in from around off, gripping and turning, catches Starc on the pads as he goes back to play at it. Big shout but the umpire remains unmoved. Sarfraz though thinks it could be close so he takes the DRS. Replays show it's missing leg stump. A leg bye is taken as the ball rolled away on the leg side.
Review taken. It's for an lbw decision against Mitchell Starc. Looks to be going down leg to the naked eye.
Quicker and shorter outside off, pushed square on the off side.

SIX! That's gone all the way. Good strike from Mitchell Starc. The wrong 'un outside off, Starc reads it well as he gets low and unleashes the big slog sweep. Connects sweetly and sends it sailing over mid-wicket.
Spinning in from around off, Starc goes back and defends. It keeps a little low too, so well played.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Tossed up on off, Jon prods forward in a solid defense.
Jon has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Almost one more for Bilal. He flights this straighter one on off. Holland plays inside the line to get beaten.
Jon Holland is the last man in for Australia.

OUT! Bowled 'em! Lovely spin bowling from Bilal Asif. He gives it a bit more air and bowls it slower. Lyon goes for the slog sweep but is completely beaten in the flight. He swings his bat a bit too early and the ball crashes into the off pole. Just one wicket more left for Australia.
Drifting down the leg is this flatter ball, worked down to the fielder at square leg.
Played to mid-wicket region by NL. One run added to the total.
Starc drills this full ball straight to long on. They cross over for a single.
Flighted ball on off, driven nicely through the covers to change strike.
Tossed up on off, driven through mid on by the batsman.
Starc sees the flighted ball on off and whacks it uppishly to long on. Takes a single.
The southpaw shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Sweep again to end the over but again he finds the fielder. A risky shot for not much of returns this.
Fuller and straighter on the stumps, worked down the leg side by Nathan.
Goes for the sweep again but this one is a bit too full for that shot. He misses and gets rapped on the pads. Given not out though as it is sliding down the leg side.
Swept again but finds the fielder at square leg.
Tossed up ball on off, swept to square leg.
Defended off the front foot by Lyon presenting the full face of the bat.
Flatter and on middle and leg this. The ball strikes the southpaw very low on the pads. The hosts are asking the question but the umpire isn't interested in the appeal.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Nathan Lyon comes in to bat next.

OUT! Run out at the non-striker's end. Really, really unlucky is Labuschagne here. One of the worst ways to get out in cricket. Shah tosses this up on off, Starc drills it straight back to Yasir who tries to stop it but just gets a finger on it before it crashes into the stumps. Pakistan appeal for a run out and the umpire has taken it upstairs. Replays roll in and show that the right-hander is a bit late in planting his bat back in the crease. Labuschagne drops his head down and walks back to the dressing room dejected.

43.4: Y Shah to Starc, OUT! Run out at the non-striker's end. Really really unfortunate is Labuschagne. One of the worst ways you can get out in cricket. Starc drives this tossed up ball on off straight back to the bowler. Yasir gets a finger on it before it crashes into the stumps at the bowler's end. A run out appeal is made by the hosts and umpire takes it upstairs. Replays roll in and show that Yasir has definitely got a finger on it and Labuschagne is a bit late getting his bat down in time. Should have reacted in time. He's gone though and Australia are in deeper trouble. Eight down.
Goes back quickly to this shortish delivery on off, punches it through point and gets a single.
Nicely flighted and around off, Labuschagne comes right forward in defense.
Very full ball on off, Starc drills it down to long on to get to the other end.
Tossed up ball around off, Labuschagne shows good composure as he blocks it out with a straight bat. Showing good confidence in his partner.
The right-hander has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Driven through the covers by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Slightly more air given to this one and lands this around off, blocked off the front foot.
A bit flatter and on middle and off, Starc pushes it back to the bowler.
Full ball on middle, Defended off the front foot.
Goes back again to this shortish delivery around off, cuts it straight to the man at point.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Played to the point region by Labuschagne, no run on offer.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. They pick up a single.

SIX! Slammed for a biggie! It was about time that the tall southpaw launches himself into one. Starc sees the ball flighted and full around off. Gets down and whacks it over mid-wicket for a superb maximum.
Short and wide outside off, Starc punches this through covers to pick up another brace.
Flighted ball on off, driven gently into the cover region for a single.
The southpaw has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
A full ball angled into his pads is flicked into the square leg region for a single by Labuschagne. Good batting this by Australia, this pair is rotating the strike nicely.
Tossed up ball and a bit outside off, driven through cover-point and changes strike.
Flighted and full on off, defended off the front foot.
Lovely shot! Wonderful use of the feet. Skips down the track to this tossed up ball on off, he reaches nicely to the pitch of the ball and caresses this through covers for three runs.
Lovely cover drive for just a single. Labuschagne leans forward and drives this full ball through covers and retains strike for the next over.
Gives this one a bit more air, Starc does well to reach to the pitch of it and drives it to mid on and takes a run.
The southpaw has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Goes back to this slower one outside off and taps it to point.
The right-hander has punched the ball off the back foot towards point. They pick up a single.
A bit too short and wide again, Labuschagne is back and cutting nicely through backward point and Hafeez has to run a long way from deep cover-point to make the sliding save. Two taken.
Defended off the back foot by Starc to finish the over.
Tossed up high, tempting the drive, he is lured in, gets a thick outside edge along the ground past second slip behind point for a brace.
The southpaw shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

FOUR! Misfield and a boundary conceded. A bit shorter this from Asif and wide of off, MS goes back and cuts it to point where the fielder completely misses the ball and allows it to races across the deep point boundary.
Flatter one on middle, it skids through and the southpaw punches it to mid on off the back foot.
Tossed up ball on off, Starc prods forward in defense.
Slower and flighted ball on off, driven to mid off.
Defended off the front foot by Marnus presenting the full face of the bat.
Goes for the slog sweep but does not time it perfectly. It goes to the man at deep mid-wicket on the bounce and the pair crosses for a single.
Starc goes back to this slower delivery on off and pushes it back to the bowler.
The southpaw has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Leg break and a bit wide of off, driven nicely out to the man stationed at the cover-point fence and gets a run.
Skips down the track to this tossed up ball on off and works it into the square leg region to retain strike.
Defended off the back foot by ML.
Flighted and full on middle and leg. The right-hander misses his front foot defense to get hit on the pads.
A bit slower this time, Labuschagne stays back and punches it back to Bilal.
Tossed right up around off, Marnus comes forward to defend but gets an inside edge to square leg.
Slower and flighted ball on off, Starc plays it into the point region off the front foot and gets off strike.
Tossed up ball on off to end the over, Labuschagne pushes it back to Yasir.
Goes back again to this shortish one around off, punches it to the man at cover-point.
Defended off the front foot by Marnus presenting the full face of the bat.
Very full ball on middle and leg, driven to short covers.
FOUR! Whacked! Tad short from Yasir outside off, ML goes back and cuts through point to get a boundary.
Almost sneaked through. Labuschagne goes back to this flatter ball on off, he gets his bat down in time to block it off the back foot.
Yasir Shah will bowl from the other end.
A bit quicker and angling into Starc. The southpaw tries to flick it into the leg side but misses to get rapped on the pads. Going down the leg was this ball.
Starts off with a tossed up ball on off, Starc comes forward and defends.

We are all set to get the afternoon session underway as the umpires along with the Pakistan team make their way to the middle. The Aussie pair of Marnus Labuschagne and Mitchell Starc stride out to the center with the latter taking strike. Bilal Asif will start proceedings and will complete his over.
... Day 2, Session 2 ...

Australia were already damaged when Paine was trapped right in front of the wickets by the offie Bilal. Pakistan are all over Australia and will now look to run through them as soon as possible after the break. Labuschagne, for the tourists, will try to get as close as possible to the Pakistan total along with the tail now. Let's see what happens on the other side of the break. Join us for all the action in a short while.

A dream session for Pakistan as they have rattled the Aussies by taking 5 wickets giving away just 71 runs in 27.4 overs. The destruction was started today by Abbas when he dismissed both Shaun Marsh and Travis Head quickly. Finch, along with Mitchell Marsh, then started to rebuild the innings but after a cautious 19-run stand, Mitchell fell prey to the guile of Yasir Shah. Bilal Asif was then introduced into the attack and he made an impact immediately taking out Finch at short leg.

OUT! Umpire's call as it is just about clipping the leg stump. End of a magnificent session for Pakistan. It is a bit quicker and flatter around off, Paine decides to go back and that proves to be his biggest error as the ball lands and spins in prodigiously. Tim looking to block it off the back foot is beaten on the inside and rapped on the pad in front of the stumps. The hosts go up in a big appeal and the umpire raises his finger after thinking for a couple of seconds. Paine thinks it might be sliding down with the spin and hence goes for the review showing the 'T'. Replays roll in and show that the impact is in line and the ball is clipping the leg stump on its way behind. That means a wicket for the home team at the stroke of the break. LUNCH ON DAY 2!
Review has been taken against an LBW decision. The batsman in question is Tim Paine. Looks close.
Similar length but a bit outside off, Paine drives it to mid off this time.
Comes forward this time to a very full ball on off, driven cleanly to mid on.
Paine goes back to this shorter delivery around off, pushes this to mid on.
A very full ball outside off, driven straight to covers.
Slower and flighted on off, kept out off the back foot.
Tossed up ball a bit outside off, Labuschagne reaches out to it but mistimes his drives back to the bowler.
Similar ball but this time the Aussie skipper goes back and punches this into the gap at cover-point to get a run.
Slower and attacking the stumps. TP goes back and blocks it out.
Tossed up ball on off. Paine prods ahead in a solid defense.
Defended off the front foot by Labuschagne presenting the full face of the bat.
Flighted ball on off, driven nicely to the right of mid on to get to the other end.
Defended off the front foot by the right-hander presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and flatter on middle and leg. Labuschagne leans across to work it through mid-wicket. They have run a single.
Better from Asif, gives this more air and keeps it full outside off. Paine comes forward and defends it into the vacant cover region to get a single.
Starts his second over, the offie, with this shortish delivery outside off. Paine cuts it to point.
Nice. Finds the gap with a neat push through the left of mid off for a brace.
Pushes this square past silly point. Dot ball.
Full, slow and on off stump, blocked off the front foot.
Short, flat and just outside off, punched off the back foot towards covers.
Stays right behind the line of this one and keeps it out.
Tossed up delivery on middle and off, driven to covers.
Tim Paine, the skipper, walks out to the middle.

OUT! Makes an impact in his very first over of the innings! Bilal Asif has got Aaron Finch. Pakistan on top of the tourists as their sixth one goes. Asif lands this full and a bit outside off, Finch comes forward to defend it, is a bit lazy as he hangs his bat in front of his pad. The ball spins in sharply, takes the inside edge onto the pads and balloons up to the left of the short leg fielder. Fakhar Zaman positioned there takes a nice catch with a dive. Big, big jolt to Australia as the hosts enter their lower order.
Nice shot. Gets well to the pitch of the ball and drives this through mid off and gets three for it.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Marnus has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Very full ball on off, Finch works it into square leg with the turn and gets off strike.
An appeal first ball by Bilal! Umpire refuses though. Overpitched outside off, and he takes a big stride forward to sweep. The ball hits him near his toes, but impact was definitely outside off.
Bilal Asif comes in to bowl for the first time in this match.
On his pads and Finch has flicked the ball through square leg. One run added to the total.
Stays back in his crease to this flatter ball on middle, punches it back to Yasir.
AF has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Flighted nicely around off, Finch drives this hard but straight to the man at short cover.
Similar ball and a similar front foot block by Aaron.
Flighted ball around off, Finch comes right ahead to defend.
A bit shorter and wide of off is this ball, Marnus plays it through the point region to take a brace.
Inside edge on the pad and into the square leg region. Aaron manages to get a faint inside edge on this which may have saved him from being an LBW candidate. A quick run is pinched.
Strays on his pads which allows Marnus to flick it to fine leg and get off strike.
Keeping it tight is Hamza. He lands this again on a length around middle and off. Labuschagne blocks it off from within his crease.
A bit fuller and attacking the stumps. ML drives it to mid off.
Length ball around off, angling across Labuschagne. He blocks it off the back foot.
Fuller but drifting down the leg side, Marnus works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
Tossed up around off, leans forward and drives it to mid on.
Loopy ball on middle and off, the youngster comes forward and keeps it out safely.
Well flighted around off, Labuschagne has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Marnus Labuschagne walks into the middle next.

OUT! Wow! Lovely, lovely leg spin bowling. Deserves this for his consistency and patience. Yasir gives this one air and keeps it full around off. Marsh lunges forward looking to block it out, the ball hits the deck and turns a bit more than he expected. Takes the outside edge and flies to Asad Shafiq at first slip who takes a good catch. Marsh's stay at the crease comes to an end. Shah is off and running.
A bit flatter and quicker one to start with, MM goes back and punches it back to Yasir.
Finch lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Well played! He waits in his crease for the ball to arrive and then taps it softly into the vacant cover-point region to change strike.
Defended off the back foot by MM.
Again a bit too short as he fires it on the middle and leg stump line. Marsh punches it to mid on.
A bit shorter but the same line. Marsh goes back in his crease to keep it out safely.
A good length ball around off, Marsh has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Finch closes his bat face a bit too early on this fuller and straighter ball on the stumps. The ball takes a leading edge but luckily for Aaron it goes into the cover region.
Very full ball on off, driven to the fielder at covers.
YS gives this one a bit more air and lands it around off. Marsh makes good use of the crease by going back and punching it through covers to get off strike.
Similar ball and an identical block by Mitch.
Tossed up ball on middle and leg, MM happy to prod forward and block.
A similar ball around off again, Finch gets his bat and pad together in a solid front foot defense.
Drags his length just that wee bit and keeps it around off, AF stands back in his crease to block it out.
Better from Hamza, attacking the stumps on a good length. Finch plays it to mid on.
Dishes this full and outside off, Finch controls himself and lets it be.
A bit wide of off stump, Aaron leaves it alone.

Starts from over the wicket and lands it on a length just outside leg. Finch tries to flick but gets hit on the thigh pad. The ball rolls into the vacant square leg region to allow the batsmen to take two leg byes.
A solid front foot defense to end the over. MM showing good composure.
Marsh has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Very full this on middle and leg, the right-hander drives it to mid off.
A bit short and outside off, MM goes back and cuts it to point.
Flighted and very full on off, Mitch is happy to push it back to where it came from.
Tossed up ball attacking the stumps, Marsh prods forward in defense.
Full ball angled into Finch, he goes for the flick but misses to get rapped on his pads. Clearly going down the leg.
Shorter again and outside off, Marsh has played it to the point region. One run added to the total.

That stayed a bit low or Mitchell's reactions at least suggests so. A good length ball this around off. Marsh goes back to block it and gets his bat down just in time as the nut hits low on his straight bat.
This time Mitch goes after this shorter ball outside off, no foot movement there and he gets a bottom edge onto the ground.
Dishes this on a good length from around the wicket, the line though is a bit too wide of off. Marsh happy to shoulder arms.
Marsh shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Mir Hamza back into the attack.

Beaten! Goes back to one which he should have come forward to. A fuller length ball around off, Finch looks to block it off the back foot, the ball lands and spins away sharply to beat his outside edge.
Similar ball and similarly defended off the front foot by the right-hander.
Full and flighted ball on off, Finch is way ahead in defense.
Aaron has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
A bit fuller this around off again. Marsh lunges forward and drives through covers to get a run.
Slower but a bit too short, allows Finch to rock back and punch it to deep cover and get to the other end.

Drinks. So a good and rewarding first hour for Pakistan as they have managed to get two important Aussie wickets. The current pair will now look to stabilize the innings and will look to bat as long as possible. The hosts will continue to put pressure on the Kangaroos by not giving away any loose balls.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

FOUR! Boom! Marsh is nailing these cover drives, that too on the up. A length ball just outside off, Mitch plants his front foot ahead and drives through the line. The timing and placement are good enough to earn him a boundary.
Wayward from Abbas as he angles this down the leg side. Sarfraz does well to dive to his left and pouch it.
A good solid front foot defense shown by Marsh, will give him some confidence.
Finch, standing a feet outside his crease may be to negate the movement, flicks this length ball angling into him through mid-wicket. The pair takes three.
A bit short and outside off this. Finch does not flirt with it.
Forces this into the off side to end the over.
FOUR! That rare loosener. Short and wide, Marsh rocks back and cuts it through point to send it across the boundary line.
The leggie is settling into good rhythm here. Very accurate today. Tosses it up on off, spins away, driven to cover.
A bit quicker through the air, Yasir keeps it around off, Mitchell defends.
Full, with a lot of air, the leg break on off. Mitchell Marsh prods forward and defends.
Looped up in line of the stumps, blocked from within the crease.

Almost, almost got him with this one. It lands on that same area on a good length around off. Marsh comes forward in defense but the ball deviates in and takes the inside edge before rolling down towards square leg. They cross over and Marsh is off the mark.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
His accuracy and consistency are admirable. He continues hitting that area around the off pole on a good length. Marsh though is good enough to come forward and defend with a straight bat.
Very full this around off. Mitch drives this gently straight back.
A bit shorter this around off, Marsh punches it to point off the back foot.
Mitchell Marsh is the next man in.

OUT! Edged and taken at second slip! Fantastic stuff from Abbas. This bowler is taking large strides as he gets another wicket to his name. Keeps it on a good length around off with the natural away angle from over the wicket. Head has to play at it because of the initial line but the ball lands and nips away. Takes the outside edge which flies to Asad Shafiq at second slip who accepts it gleefully. Australia four down now.
Down the track again and driven to covers to take a quick single.
If he missed this block he was a candidate for LBW. Yasir lands this full on middle, Finch leans on his front foot to work it towards square leg and get a run.
Aaron has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
This time he goes back and works it into the square leg region to get a single. Smart batting, this. Rotating the strike well.
A bit shorter on off, goes back and punches it to mid off.

FOUR! Down the track and bang! Head tries to counter-attack and does well. Skips out to this flighted ball in line with the stumps. Gets nicely under it to whack it over mid-wicket for his first boundary.
Length ball on middle and leg, flicked to mid-wicket by the attacking right-hander.
Full again and attacking the stumps, Aaron drives it crisply to mid off.
Good bowling and well played. A fuller length ball around off, Finch does well to solidly defend it with bat and pad close together.
Defended off the front foot by Finch presenting the full face of the bat.

Whipped for another three. A rare wayward delivery from the medium pacer as he dishes out this length ball on Head's pads. The southpaw gets nicely inside the line of it and flicks it through square leg to earn three more runs.
Good shot. Fractionally shorter outside off, the length and the width allow Finch to stand tall and punch it through cover-point off the front foot. Gets three for it.
Head charges down the wicket and drives this loopy ball to mid off.
Goes for the sweep to this very full and flighted ball on leg, mistimes it to square leg.
Still attacking the leg stump line, Head goes back to punch it to mid-wicket.
Fuller and attacking the stumps, worked into the leg side by the southpaw.
Similar ball this from over the wicket, Head flicks it to square leg.
Tossed up ball on the leg stump line to start off from the leggie. Pushed into the mid-wicket region.
Yasir Shah comes in to bowl for the first time today.
A bit too short this, Finch ducks under it comfortably.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

Big appeal, first for the LBW and then for the catch at gully. A bit too high this and no bat involved. Deadly accurate is Abbas and he is asking a lot of questions to the Aussie batsmen. Keeps this one marginally shorter of a good length around off, it hits a crack and deviates in prodigiously to beat Finch's bat on the inside and raps him high on the front pad. The hosts go up in a big appeal but it is given not out by the umpire.
Fuller delivery this on middle and off, Finch pushes it back to the bowler.
Length ball around off, Aaron prods ahead in defense.

Fires that on a length but it's angling on his pads, Finch tries to flick but gets hit on the thigh pad. The ball rolls towards square leg and the right-hander takes off for a quick single before being sent back rightfully by his partner.
A very full ball around off is played to mid on with a straight bat.
A bit of an inward angle on this one, a bit too much maybe as he drifts on Head's pads. Travis flicks it towards square leg to get a couple more.
Similar ball and the southpaw is happy to watchfully block it out on the off side.
A bit fuller from Hamza around off, Head lunges forward nicely to defend it.
Good length ball on off, shaping into Head, the southpaw pushes it to the left of mid on and gets a brace.
Surprises the batsman with a change in length. Bangs this one very short. Finch pulls it onto the ground from over head height. Gets one for it.
Shaping into middle and off, he turns this with the angle to mid-wicket and a misfield allows a single for the right-hander to retain strike.
On the pads, helped to fine leg to get off the mark. The southpaw needs to come up with a good show here, his team needs it now.
Fuller around off, looking to get that slight movement. The ball though goes straight on as Head defends off the front foot this time.
Pulls his line a bit straighter, attacking the middle and leg pole from over the wicket. Head pushes it towards mid on.
A bit fuller this but Head still waits back inside his crease to keep it out.
That's a good first ball to a new batsman. Keeps it on a good length around off, angling away from Head. The southpaw blocks it tentatively from the crease.
Continues with the line and the right-handed opener is happy to shoulder arms to it.
Aaron lets the ball go outside his off stump.
In the corridor around off, Finch comes forward in a solid defense.
Shorter in length again and attacking the stumps, Finch punches this to mid on from within his crease.
A bit too wide of off to entice Aaron into a false shot. He leaves it.

Starts the new over from around the wicket and lands it a bit short of a good length outside off. Finch throws his hands at it without moving his feet and misses the ball. Needs to focus more, they cannot afford to lose one more so soon.
Travis Head to bat next.

OUT! Edged and taken! Shaun Marsh's short stay in the middle comes to an end. It's Mohammad Abbas again who provides the breakthrough for his side. Lands it on off, it moves away ever so late and this becomes Shaun Marsh's undoing. The ball takes the outside edge of his hanging bat and flies to first slip, where Haris Sohail moves to his right and pouches it safely.
Nice and tight, full on off, Marsh comes forward and meets it with the full face of the bat.
Quite full and straight in line, worked down in front of square leg. Bit of a nervous start from Marsh, not looking too confident at the moment.
Shaping away from around off, Marsh raises his bat and lets it be.
On the fuller side of things, on off stump, blocked out with a straight bat.
That kept really low. Went to Sarfraz almost rolling along the turf. Abbas hurls it across, outside off, goes past the outside edge and to Sarfraz.
Angling in on off, blocked with a tight defense.
Pushes this tamely to the same area, but finds the fielder this time.
FOUR! Third one of the morning from Finch. He's nailing those cover drives to perfection. Leans into the full ball and finds the gap through the covers with ease.
Hangs on the back foot and keeps it out safely.

Almost dragged it on! That was CLOSE. Wow. Would have been the ideal start for Mir Hamza and Pakistan. It's on a length with some width outside off, Shaun Marsh just wants to crash this through the off side, so he goes back to cut. Ends up getting an inside edge which bounces past the off stump and goes behind towards fine leg. Three runs taken.
Fired in full, outside the line of off stump, driven to mid off for nothing.
This full delivery is eased down the ground towards mid on.
Better. Abbas drags his length a touch shorter, it's just outside off. Aaron covers the line and shoulders arms.
Keeps the line a little straighter, on middle, blocked with the full face of the bat.
Good length ball close to off, defended from within the crease.
FOUR! Beautiful. Holding the pose for the cameras too. Full in length and outside off, Aaron Finch leans into the drive and caresses it through the gap in the covers to find the fence.
Keeps it full and just outside off, driven off the inner half on the leg side.
Mohammad Abbas will bowl from the other end.
Stays back and keeps this length ball out on the off side.
Drives this full ball to mid on and gets to the other end.
Full and straight, Finch keeps bat and pad close together to block this out.
Ahead of a length, just outside off, blocked out in front of covers.
FOUR! Shot. Too good. Full and well outside off, Finch has room to work with so he strides forward and drives this on the up through the covers for a boundary.
Angling across from outside off, a harmless delivery, Finch lets it be.

Out come the players to begin things on this hot, sunny day. Aaron Finch strides out with a new partner, Shaun Marsh. Mir Hamza to begin proceedings with the new ball first. Two slips and a gully in place. Here we go...

After a 12-wicket first day of this Test ensured that the game has progressed ahead in full speed, it was a roller-coaster ride with both teams winning various passages of play throughout the day and gaining and losing control on the game. In the first hour of the day Nathan Lyon bamboozled the hosts' top order by picking a 4-wicket haul. But then a massive 147-run stand between Zaman and Sarfraz saw them pull things back and even ahead a bit, as Pakistan posted 282 on the board and bagged 2 Aussie wickets before Stumps. They will want to build on that and make further inroads into the Australian batting line-up at the earliest. The Kangaroos, on the flip side, will hope for a solid batting performance today and gain a first innings lead by end of day. It sure is going to be an intense battle to get a better grip on the match.
... Day 2, Session 1 ...

Australia have started their innings on a wobbly note. The unfortunate wicket of Khawaja, caught down the leg side, and then the dismissal of the nightwatchman Siddle on the last ball of the day has put the tourists on the back foot. Their batsmen will look to occupy the crease for a longer duration of time on Day 2 and try to get a decent lead. Join us at 1000 local (0600 GMT) for all the action. Cheers!

Earlier, Pakistan fought back well after an initial collapse to get their total up to 282. Nathan Lyon was simply unplayable in the first session but made no impact after that. The surprise package of the day was Marnus Labuschagne, who was brought on by Paine to get a breakthrough and that's exactly what he did. The leggie got three and managed to restrict the  hosts below 300.

A fairly even first day of this Test, however, you can argue that it is slightly tilting in favor of Pakistan. They have managed to close off the day, which did not start on an ideal note for them in the first session, on a high.

OUT! Abbas strikes on the very last ball of the day. What a brilliant way to end the day for Pakistan. Abbas dishes this on a good length around off, Siddle again looks to block this off from within his crease. The ball hits the deck and deviates into the batsman. It beats Siddle's tentative push on the inside and raps him flush on the pads in front of the stumps. It's very close as Pakistan go up in a huge appeal. Surprisingly, the umpire turns it down. Sarfraz does not wait any time and goes for the review. replays roll in and display three reds on the screen which means that Siddle will not come out to bat tomorrow morning. That is STUMPS ON DAY 1.
Review taken by Pakistan for an LBW decision. The batsman in question is Peter Siddle.
Attacks the stumps with a good length delivery, Siddle though does well to keep it out from his crease.
Just too wide of off to entice the batsman into a shot.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat. Three more to go for the day.
Fires this full and wide of off, Peter shoulders arms to let that one through.
Bouncer! Gets the short ball to rise sharply onto the batsman. Siddle does well to sway away from the line by leaning back.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot. Australia have survived the Yasir threat for the day.
Similar ball is dealt with similarly by playing it towards point.
Goes back to this loopy ball in line with the stumps, Finch taps it into the point region off the back foot.
Tossed up ball again around off, Finch watchfully blocks it out off the back foot.
Defended off the front foot by the Aaron presenting the full face of the bat.
Flighted outside off, Finch shoulders arms to let that one through.
Abbas attacking the stumps drifts slightly down leg. Siddle plays it down the leg side and picks up a brace for it.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Waits for this flatter and a bit shorter ball outside off, opens the bat face and glides it through the point region to get a brace.
Siddle has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Peter Siddle, the nightwatchman, comes in to bat.

OUT! Pakistan have drawn first blood. A bit lucky but this but a really good grab by the Pakistan captain. The hero from the last match has to walk back to the pavilion. Abbas keeps it on a good length on middle and leg and angling into the batsman. Khawaja looks to flick it but the ball takes the faintest of nicks and flies behind down the leg side. Sarfraz dives to his right fully stretched and pouches this low and one handed. The umpires want to check if the catch is clean and they go upstairs with the soft signal as out. Replays roll in and show that the edge carries easily to Sarfraz behind. This is also the 50th Test wicket for Abbas.
Both the umpires have a chat regarding a catch down the leg side and decide to go upstairs.
Abbas starts the over from around the wicket. Lands this full around off, Usman drives it to covers from the crease.
FOUR! That's smashed away. Tossed up right in the slot, Finch stands his ground and lofts it powerfully over mid off for a boundary.
Slows this up as he bowls it full and just outside off, blocked from the front foot.
Khawaja drills this full delivery down the ground and gets to the other end.
Darted in full and quick, flicked past short mid-wicket by Finch for a single.
Walks down the track and flicks it to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Full and quick on off, Usman with a tame push on the off side.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

FOUR! Nudged very fine onto the leg side for the first boundary of the innings. Abbas errs in line and fires this down the leg side. Finch does well to get some bat on it and to tickle it fine down the leg side to cross the rope there.
Fuller on middle and leg stump line, Finch flicks it away with a wristy shot.

Big appeal for an LBW, given not out though. That is some good seam bowling from Abbas. He lands this on a good length on off. The ball nips back in to beat Finch's forward defense and rap him on the pads. The Pakistan team go up in an appeal in unison, the umpire refuses and the hosts decide not to go for the review.
Dishes this a bit fuller on off, Usman drives it towards mid off and gets a quick run for it.
Continues in that corridor around off, Khawaja has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
On a good length again and straight in line with the stumps, Finch flicks it towards square leg.

Not out. Finch goes for the pull to this short of a length ball angling into his body. The ball though rises a bit more than he expects on him. Gets the gloves and rolls fine towards fine leg. The batsmen run back for a second as the fielder throws it back to Sarfraz who takes the bails off and appeals for a run out. Replays show that Finch is comfortably in.
The third umpire called into action for a run out appeal against Aaron Finch. He looks safe though.
Fires this one on his pads, Finch works it onto the leg side.
A bit fuller and outside off, Finch drives this through covers to get a brace.
Starts with a good length ball around off from over the wicket. Finch defends off the back foot and with a straight bat.
Mir Hamza to bowl from the other end.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Rising off the deck, from a good length, Khawaja manages to defend it off the top half of the bat down on the off side.
Stays back and keeps it out off the back foot.
A bit further away from the off stick, another leave from the batsman.
Shaping away from around off, on a good length once more, Khawaja lets it be.
Length delivery on middle and off, Khawaja defends it well from inside the crease.
